decision.summary: The Federal Reserve kept the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent while speeding up the reduction of its bond purchases.

changes.quote: Job gains have been solid in recent months, and the unemployment rate has declined substantially.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this point to highlight that the job market has made strong progress.

changes.quote: Supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic and the reopening of the economy have continued to contribute to elevated levels of inflation.
changes.explanation: The Fed updated its language to show that high inflation is continuing due to pandemic supply and demand mismatches.

changes.quote: In light of inflation developments and the further improvement in the labor market, the Committee decided to reduce the monthly pace of its net asset purchases by $20 billion for Treasury securities and $10 billion for agency mortgage-backed securities.
changes.explanation: The Fed accelerated the tapering of its bond-buying program in response to strong employment and high inflation.

changes.quote: Beginning in January, the Committee will increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $40 billion per month and of agency mortgage-backed securities by at least $20 billion per month.
changes.explanation: This specifies the exact lower monthly amount of new bonds the Fed will buy starting in January.

changes.quote: Risks to the economic outlook remain, including from new variants of the virus.
changes.explanation: The Fed explicitly noted that new variants of the virus continue to pose risks to the economy.

tone_quotes.quote: Job gains have been solid in recent months, and the unemployment rate has declined substantially.

With inflation having exceeded 2 percent for some time, the Committee expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 14.54% APR costs about $60.58 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.47% and moved +3 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.11% would rise by about $4.90 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 639k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 6.9% over the past year (November 2021); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 4.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +2 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 1.63%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.16% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed is moving faster to wrap up its bond purchases in response to high inflation and stronger employment. Educational forecast models suggest an 83% chance of a rate hike at upcoming meetings.

citations.detail: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.
